config.title: Position: relative and absolute

intro.title: Position: relative and absolute
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout to understand how CSS positioning works. You will learn the core concepts of 'position: relative' and 'position: absolute' to precisely control where elements appear on the page. The main technologies involved are CSS properties for positioning and HTML for structure. By the end, you'll be able to move elements relative to their normal position or to a parent container, creating layered and dynamic designs.
intro.usecase: Positioning with relative and absolute is essential for creating precise, layered UI components in real-world applications. For example, developers use these properties to build custom tooltips that appear anchored to a button, or to place a notification badge precisely in the corner of a user avatar. In product dashboards, absolute positioning is key for overlaying status indicators on data cards, while relative positioning helps align form labels and error messages directly next to their input fields. Mastering these techniques allows you to implement complex layouts like dropdown menus, modals, and interactive panels that are common in modern web interfaces.

objectives: Apply the position: relative property to establish a positioning context for child elements
Configure the position: absolute property to precisely place elements within a relative container
Manipulate element placement using top, right, bottom, and left offset properties
Construct overlapping visual layouts by controlling the stacking order with z-index
Implement relative positioning to adjust an element's position without affecting document flow
Integrate absolute positioning to create positioned elements that scroll with their container
Initialize a positioning context by setting a parent element to position: relative

steps.title: Create a container element with basic styling
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' that sets width to 500px, height to 400px, and background color to #f0f0f0.
steps.hint: Use the class selector .container followed by curly braces. Inside, add the width, height, and background-color properties with the specified values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .container with the specified dimensions and background color is created.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .container selector with width: 500px, height: 400px, and background-color: #f0f0f0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some properties are missing or incorrect. Make sure you have width: 500px, height: 400px, and background-color: #f0f0f0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .container is not correct. Please create a .container class with width: 500px, height: 400px, and background-color: #f0f0f0.

steps.title: Add a child element inside the container
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a child element with the class name 'box' inside your container. This will be the element we'll position relative to the container later.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule starting with '.box' and add some basic styling like background color and dimensions.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create your container styling here */

/* Add your .box styling here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for the .box class is added with some basic styling properties.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .box selector with at least one styling property (like background-color, width, or height).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a CSS rule, but make sure it uses the exact class name '.box' and includes at least one styling property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't contain a properly formatted .box rule. Check that you're using the correct selector syntax and adding styling properties.

steps.title: Style the child element with basic properties
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to the .box selector to give it a width of 100px, height of 100px, a background color of lightblue, and a 2px solid black border.
steps.hint: Use the properties width, height, background-color, and border. Remember to include units (px) for width and height.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will become a visible square with a light blue fill and a black border, making it distinct from the container.
successCriteria: The .box selector has width: 100px;, height: 100px;, background-color: lightblue;, and border: 2px solid black;.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but check if all required properties (width, height, background-color, border) are present with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box element needs all four properties: width, height, background-color, and border. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Apply position: relative to the container
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property `position: relative;` to your container element's styling.
steps.hint: This establishes a positioning context for any absolutely positioned child elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now serve as a reference point for positioning child elements.
successCriteria: The container element's CSS includes `position: relative;`
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added `position: relative;` to the container element's styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container element needs `position: relative;` to establish a positioning context for child elements.

steps.title: Apply position: absolute to the child element
steps.instruction: Add position: absolute to the .box element's CSS rules.
steps.hint: Use the position property with the value absolute inside the .box selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will be positioned absolutely relative to its nearest positioned ancestor (the container with position: relative).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added position: absolute; to the .box CSS rules.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box element needs position: absolute; to be positioned absolutely within its relative parent.

steps.title: Position the absolute element using top and left
steps.instruction: Add the CSS properties `top: 20px` and `left: 30px` to the `.box` rule to position it relative to its container.
steps.hint: Inside the `.box` selector, add `top: 20px;` and `left: 30px;` on new lines after the `position: absolute;` declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The absolutely positioned box will be offset 20 pixels from the top and 30 pixels from the left of its relatively positioned container.
successCriteria: The `.box` selector includes both `top: 20px;` and `left: 30px;` properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both `top: 20px;` and `left: 30px;` properties to the `.box` rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the correct CSS properties with the specified values inside the `.box` selector.

steps.title: Add a second child element with position: absolute
steps.instruction: Add a second div element with class 'box2' inside your container element in the HTML structure.
steps.hint: You'll need to add another <div> tag with class='box2' as a sibling to the existing .box element.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your HTML structure will have two child elements (.box and .box2) inside the container, both ready to be absolutely positioned.
successCriteria: A second div with class 'box2' exists as a child element inside the container in your HTML structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div with class='box2' inside your container element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second element wasn't added correctly. You need to add a div with class='box2' as a sibling to the existing .box element.

steps.title: Position the second element using bottom and right
steps.instruction: Add bottom: 40px and right: 50px to the second absolutely positioned box.
steps.hint: Use the bottom and right properties to position the second box relative to its container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second box will be positioned 40px from the bottom and 50px from the right of its container.
successCriteria: The second box has bottom: 40px and right: 50px applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both bottom: 40px and right: 50px to the second box.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second box doesn't have the correct positioning. It needs bottom: 40px and right: 50px.

steps.title: Add a third element without position: absolute
steps.instruction: Add a third div element with class 'normal-box' inside the container element in your HTML structure. This element should not have any position property applied to it, so it remains in the normal document flow.
steps.hint: Create a new div element with class='normal-box' and place it inside the same container that holds your .box and .second-box elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A third div element with class 'normal-box' appears inside the container, positioned according to the normal document flow (not using position: absolute).
successCriteria: The HTML contains a div element with class='normal-box' inside the container element, and no position property is applied to it in the CSS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the element, but make sure it's inside the same container as the other boxes and doesn't have any position property applied.
steps.feedbackWrong: The third element is missing or incorrectly placed. Add a div with class='normal-box' inside the container element without any position property.

steps.title: Observe the layout behavior
steps.instruction: Add a comment above the normal-box styling to describe how the absolutely positioned elements overlap it and are positioned relative to the container.
steps.hint: Write a CSS comment that explains the layout behavior you see when viewing the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: A comment is added that describes the layout behavior of absolute positioning relative to the container.
successCriteria: A CSS comment is present above the normal-box styling that mentions absolute positioning, overlap, and relative positioning to the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Your comment is on the right track. Make sure it specifically mentions how the absolutely positioned elements overlap the normal flow element and are positioned relative to the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comment doesn't fully describe the layout behavior. Try writing a comment that explains how absolute positioning affects element positioning and overlap.
